angles.title: accountant-write-scope (authz boundary violated by a shared read helper)

droppedAngles.title: migrations-and-rollout
droppedAngles.why: No schema or data migration is touched (src/migrations is untouched); the new role is just a string value on an existing `role` field with no new column, deploy-order dependency, or backfill. Old and new code read the same `role` field identically.

droppedAngles.title: data-integrity
droppedAngles.why: No concurrency, caching, or retry logic is touched by this diff — canSee and getOwnAccount are synchronous, side-effect-free reads over the in-memory store; the only writes reachable (close, deposit) already existed and are unchanged in their own concurrency behavior.

droppedAngles.title: silent-drops
droppedAngles.why: No new field is written anywhere in this diff. `role: 'accountant'` is stored and read through the exact same `users` schema key as `admin`/`member` (src/store.js SCHEMA.users includes 'role'), and publicUser already serializes it. Nothing is written and silently dropped.

scoutNotes: The PR adds an `accountant` role and a `canSee(user, account)` helper used inside the shared `getOwnAccount(store, user, id)` to let an accountant read any account by id. But `getOwnAccount` is the single gate behind four routes — GET account, GET transfers, POST close, and POST export — not just the two read routes the PR's own test exercises, so the widened check also widens the write route (`closeAccount`) and the file-writing route (`exportTransfers`).

confirmed.title: Accountant role can close and export others' accounts
confirmed.rootCause: canSee()'s accountant exception was folded into the single getOwnAccount() helper that every by-id account route shares for authorization, so closeAccount() (POST /accounts/:id/close) and the export route (POST /accounts/:id/export) inherit the relaxed ownership check and let an accountant irreversibly close or export any member's zero-balance account, contradicting the PR's own documented 'accountant ... change nothing / not an administrator' contract (confirmed by reproduction: an accountant token closed and exported another member's account, both returning HTTP 200).
confirmed.summary: canSee()/getOwnAccount() is the single gate shared by every account route, including the two write/state-changing routes (POST /accounts/:id/close and POST /accounts/:id/export), so granting accountant unconditional read-access via canSee also grants it unconditional access to those writes, contradicting the documented 'accountant | read any account and its transfers; change nothing' role.
confirmed.failure: With an accountant-role token (not the owner, not an admin), POST /accounts/:id/close on another member's zero-balance account returns 200 and durably closes it (closed:true persists and is visible to the owner afterward); POST /accounts/:id/export on the same foreign account returns 200 and writes a CSV file for that account to the server's exports directory on disk.

foundBy: accountant-write-scope (authz boundary violated by a shared read helper)
confirmed.reasoning: Read src/accounts.js and src/server.js: closeAccount() (called from POST /accounts/:id/close) and the export route handler (POST /accounts/:id/export) both call getOwnAccount(store, user, id) with no additional ownership/role check of their own — the same helper used by the GET routes. getOwnAccount now gates via canSee(), which returns true for any user with role === 'accountant' regardless of account ownership. requireUser only checks the caller is signed in; requireRole (used only for POST /deposits) is not applied to close or export. I reproduced this live: created an account as member tok-bob (zero balance), then as accountant tok-eve called POST /accounts/:id/close -> HTTP 200 with closed:true, durably persisted (confirmed by a follow-up GET as tok-bob, the real owner, which also shows closed:true). Then POST /accounts/:id/export as tok-eve -> HTTP 200, and a CSV file was actually written to disk under the exports directory for that foreign account. Before this diff, getOwnAccount required strict account.ownerId === user.id, which would have 404'd both calls for a non-owner, non-admin actor — so this escalation is introduced by this diff. The PR's one new test only covers GET /accounts/:id and GET /accounts/:id/transfers, leaving this uncaught, exactly as claimed. All six site line numbers (accounts.js:42/44/48/49, appearing twice each) correspond exactly to getOwnAccount's definition/check and closeAccount's definition/call into it — all consistent with this one real, reproduced defect; no false sites.
confirmed.panel: 3 of 3 skeptics could not refute it

missed.what: The PR's stated purpose is reconciliation — an accountant reading accounts to check them — but the one endpoint that would let an accountant *discover* which accounts exist, GET /accounts, was not touched and still calls listAccounts(store, { ownerId: user.id, page }) (src/server.js:45), which filters strictly on a.ownerId === ownerId (src/accounts.js:27-34). An accountant's own id matches no account, so this route returns an empty page for them regardless of how many accounts exist. Verified empirically: with two accounts opened by other users, GET /accounts as the accountant returns {"total":0,"items":[]}. So the only way an accountant can exercise the new canSee grant is to already know an account's id from some out-of-band source — the feature as merged cannot be used to survey the ledger, which is the whole point of a reconciliation role. This sits in an unmodified function in the very file the diff edits, so a diff-scoped read naturally skips it, and it's an under-grant (missing capability) rather than an over-grant, which is the opposite direction from every listed angle. The existing unit test 'listing is paged, newest first, and only the owner's' (test/accounts.test.js) locks in the owner-only filter and was left unchanged, and the new integration test only ever fetches an already-known account id, so nothing exercises or notices the gap.
missed.why: accountant-write-scope and security look for the role gaining access it shouldn't, not capability the role never gets despite the spec promising it. authz-and-attribution and boundary-contract check that the permission boundary is drawn correctly on existing checks, not whether a second, unmodified endpoint in the same subsystem was left out of the feature entirely. tests-that-dont-test would need to assert on list/discovery behavior for the new role to surface this, but the one new test only ever reads a single pre-known account id, so reviewing that test's quality doesn't point at a different, untouched route. correctness over the diff's own hunks can't flag an omission that lives outside those hunks. migrations-and-rollout, data-integrity and silent-drops (correctly ruled out) are also not about missing read paths.
